To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the transverse momentum distribution of hadrons from jets is shifted by the fluid flow to larger pt values, with a shift that increases with pt, (ii) the shift is of the same order of magnitude as the one from the standard parton energy loss, (iii) the shift is not a simple additive shift, but depends strongly on the fluid velocity, (iv) the shift is larger in the out direction, and (v) the shift is largest for intermediate pt hadrons

(i) The jet hadrons from the fluid have a larger pt than the jet hadrons from flux tube breaking; (ii) the jet hadrons produced by the fluid have a harder spectrum than the jet hadron spectrum from the vacuum, and (iii) the jet hadron yield from the fluid is larger than from the vacuum.
the parton momentum distributions in the fluid, and the fluid velocity at freeze-out, play an important role for the jet hadronization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) the physics of jet production in the framework of the partonic energy loss approach, and the interplay between jets and the bulk medium, with emphasis on the production of jet hadrons at intermediate pt; (ii) jet quenching in the presence of a strong magnetic field, and (iii) the physics of jets in the framework of a new theoretical approach, the partonic energy-loss approach.
the following issues: 1) How to separate bulk matter and jets, in order to be able to describe both in the same framework.
the interplay between the bulk matter and the jet hadrons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present scheme is able to account for bulk matter and jets, and their interaction, in a consistent manner.
jets are produced in the bulk, and are then pushed out by the fluid, but that the bulk also contributes to the jet hadrons.

the present model provides a reasonable description of the available data, and is consistent with a scenario where jets and bulk matter are produced in a unified picture, and where the jet production mechanism is not the same for low and high pt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a scheme to separate jets from bulk matter, and we are in the process of calculating jet spectra and nuclear modification factors for the LHC.
we have a consistent picture of jets from bulk matter that is in agreement with all the relevant experimental data.

we have developed a new approach for the study of jets in heavy ion collisions, which is based on a realistic description of both the jet production and the bulk medium, and the interaction of jets with bulk matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fluid may be the source of the quark- antiquark needed for flux tube breaking and jet production, and that this may have an effect on the pt spectrum of jet hadrons, especially for intermediate pt.
the jets may be produced in the bulk matter, with a substantial contribution to the jet hadrons.
the jet hadrons from the fluid are expected to be more isotropic than those from the jet core.
